kaizen.heading: Kaizen
kaizen.lead: A Pomodoro timer with Focus Rooms, where you study next to other people without a camera.
kaizen.story: I started building Kaizen in September 2025, based on something I kept seeing in the study community I run on Discord: people focus better when someone else is there. That community now has about 30,000 members. It came out on Google Play on 2 January 2026, on the web later that month, and on the App Store and the Microsoft Store in May.
kaizen.figures: More than {signups} people have signed up so far, and together they have logged more than {hours} hours of focus. The app averages {rating} stars on the App Store and Google Play.
kaizen.figuresSource: Sign-ups and hours from Kaizen’s admin panel, {date}.
inside: One Expo codebase in TypeScript for iOS, Android and the web, wrapped for Windows in a Tauri shell written in Rust.
App blocking through native modules I wrote in Kotlin and Swift.
Offline-first sync on Supabase that keeps several devices in step.
Property-based and mutation tests on the sync and stats logic. CI fails below an 80 percent mutation score.

caseStudy.lede: Kaizen is a Pomodoro timer with Focus Rooms: you study next to other people, without a camera or a microphone. I build and run it on my own. This page is about how it is made, including a release that went wrong.

tour.title: Timer
tour.body: Work and break sessions over a background you pick. It keeps time with the screen off, and on Android a notification shows the countdown, with pause and skip.
tour.alt: The timer screen: a focus session over an illustrated sunset

tour.title: Focus Rooms
tour.body: Rooms of 2 to 50 people, each on their own timer. The room shows who is focusing, who is on a break and who stepped away.
tour.alt: A Focus Room with six members and their timers

tour.title: Tasks
tour.body: A one-line Inbox for quick capture and a To Do list for what you have committed to. Minutes from the timer go to the task you picked as your focus task.
tour.alt: The task list with an Inbox, To Do items and time estimates

tour.title: Habits
tour.body: Habits with schedules, and streaks that survive a planned rest day. Focus-time habits fill up from the timer by themselves.
tour.alt: The habit list with a week strip and three habits

tour.title: App blocking
tour.body: Pick the apps that distract you and they stay blocked while a work session runs. A break lifts the block until the next session.
tour.alt: The block screen: Reddit is paused until blocking is turned off

tour.title: Statistics
tour.body: A daily streak, focus time by hour and weekday, and a history where you can re-tag or delete a past session.
tour.alt: A profile with a 42-day streak and focus statistics

caseStudy.end: Questions about any of this? Email me at {email}.
